sentences.text: To safely drain a node, configure a PodDisruptionBudget (optionally setting `AlwaysAllow` Unhealthy Pod Eviction Policy), then run `kubectl drain` (which respects the budget and ignores certain system pods), and if DaemonSet pods exist, include `--ignore-daemonsets`; after the command succeeds, power down or delete the node and later run `kubectl uncordon` to resume scheduling.

citations.quote: It is recommended to set `AlwaysAllow` Unhealthy Pod Eviction Policy to your PodDisruptionBudgets
You can use `kubectl drain` to safely evict all of your pods from a node... will respect the PodDisruptionBudgets you have specified
If there are pods managed by a DaemonSet, you will need to specify `--ignore-daemonsets` with `kubectl` to successfully drain the node
